title: Who writes it, and who is allowed to change it?

title: How long should an instruction be before it stops being read properly?

title: What belongs in a standing instruction versus in the request itself?

title: How do you tell an instruction that is working from one everybody ignores?
snippet: Capture actual loaded version and step/use observations, then compare outcome/adherence against controls; being present in context does not prove it influenced behavior.

title: What happens when two instructions conflict, and which wins?

title: How is an instruction tested before it is relied on?
snippet: Test valid, malformed, conflicting, stale and injected-source cases plus clean controls before relying on a bundle; preserve exact runtime and evidence dependencies.

title: How would you know an instruction had quietly stopped being followed?

title: How does a fixed path handle the case it did not anticipate?

title: How does a decided path avoid wandering?

snippet: Resume only from compatible accepted checkpoints with current input/authority/validity and reconciled effects; captured results replay as data while regeneration is a new attempt.

title: How long may a single run take before something is wrong?

title: Which stages can be skipped and which never?

title: What happens to work that sits in one stage too long?

title: Should different kinds of work have different stages?

title: How much ceremony is worth it for small work?

title: What does the stage tell you that the status does not?
snippet: Stage describes business/evidence maturity such as investigated or deliverable; status describes running, waiting or finished and cannot imply maturity by itself.

title: Who is allowed to move something backwards?

title: When should a worker do something itself rather than hand it on?

title: How deep should that go before nobody can follow it?

title: What happens when a delegated worker fails or never returns?

title: How do you stop delegation being used to avoid a hard judgement?
